title: Gowers norm bound for functions far from low degree
statement:
Let $d \ge 1$ and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function that is $\varepsilon$-far from degree $\le d$, meaning $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$ and $\dist(f, g) \ge \varepsilon$ for every Boolean function $g$ of degree $\le d$. Then there is a constant $c > 0$ for which the $\pm 1$ lift $(-1)^{f}$ satisfies
\[
  \bigl\|(-1)^{f}\bigr\|_{U^{d+1}}^{2^{d+1}} \;\le\; 1 - c\,\varepsilon.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is ε-far from degree ≤ d (which includes 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1 and dist(f,g) ≥ ε for all degree-≤d g)
replaced:
If $d \ge 1$ and $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from degree $\le d$, then there exists
a constant $c > 0$ such that
$\|(-1)^f\|_{U^{d+1}}^{2^{d+1}} \le 1 - c\varepsilon$.
For $d = 1$ one may take $c = 2$; the case $d \ge 2$ follows by induction using
the derivative distance lemma (BKSSZ 2010).
